title: MMPack: Multi-Mask Co-Design for Ultra-Large Wafer-Scale Package Integration
problem: Ultra-large wafer-scale integration requires multi-mask lithography for manufacturing, introducing physical design constraints, mask stitching discontinuities, and thermo-mechanical stress near TSVs and stitching regions that conventional floorplanning methods fail to address.
motivation: Advanced AI/HPC systems demand large-scale chiplet integration; reliable physical design methods are critical for managing complexity, yield, and thermal reliability in wafer-scale systems.
method: MMPack partitions an ultra-large chip into smaller sections (chiplets) arranged to minimize communication crossing mask boundaries—the seams where different manufacturing masks connect. Using hierarchical layout planning with alternating optimization (iteratively refining different parts of the design), it respects manufacturing constraints imposed by these seams. Finally, it applies physics models to identify high-stress regions near mask seams and through-silicon vias (vertical connections between layers), then redesigns them to reduce thermal and mechanical stress.
key_novelty: MMPack is the first framework that jointly optimizes for both the manufacturing constraints of splitting chips across multiple production masks and the thermal-mechanical stress (damage from heat-induced material expansion) that concentrates at mask seams in ultra-large wafer-scale integration.
contributions: Performance-driven partitioning algorithm for multi-mask integration
Demonstrated scalability for large wafer-scale systems

metrics.ppa: Enhanced architectural performance and mechanical reliability
metrics.other: Improved layout quality and runtime scalability

limitations: Evaluation limited to benchmark designs; real wafer-scale system validation not demonstrated; thermal-stress tradeoff not extensively explored.
